santiago: Heads up — ran an nsys trace on a customer repro and found a surprising KV write hotspot during decoding. timeline: https://perf.redwood/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:

morgan: link looks like the write kernels are dominating? can you paste the top kernels + sample timeline snippet?

santiago: quick paste from nsys summary (trimmed):
```
GPU activities:
- fused_attn_v2_kernel         42.1 ms  (41%)
- kv_cache_write_kernel       33.8 ms  (33%)
- memcpy_h2d                 10.2 ms  (10%)
- other                      17.0 ms  (16%)
Total GPU time ~103.1 ms
```
Timeline shows repeated short bursts of kv writes interleaved with fused-attn, causing stalls on warp sched.

sarah: what was batch/seq/config?

santiago: batch=2, beam=4, seq_len=1536, model=redwood/open-6b-ish, kernel_policy=`auto` (prefers fused), kv stored as fp16 contiguous [B,heads,seq,dim_head].

perf-bot: nsys run complete — job=1853004321 — /artifacts/nsys/1853004321.nsys-rep (uploaded) :white_check_mark:

alex: spike looks like bank conflicts on the KV write tile. fused_attn_v2 uses 128x4 tiling for KV writes. With seq len 1536 and batch=2 those tiles misalign -> many partial-writes. can you grab l1/lds/store-stall counters?

jesse: ran ncu counters on smaller repro:
```
ncu --target-processes all --metrics l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_stalled_cycles,sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active
Result:
- l1tex_stall_cycles: 12.3M
- tensor_cycles_active: 9.7M
```
high stall ratio on L1 for the write kernels.

morgan: hmm could also be layout vs vector-store width. fused kernel writes 128-bit stores; if tensor dims not 16-byte aligned we get read-modify-write?

santiago: exact repro command I used: 
```
./run_decode --model open-6b --batch 2 --beam 4 --seq 1536 --kernel-policy auto --profile nsys --out /tmp/trace
```
and kernel policy config snippet:
```
kernel_selection:
  mode: auto
  heuristics:
    prefer: ["fused_v2", "flash"]    # current
    fallback_on: ["seq_len>1024", "l1_stall>10pct"]
```

morgan: try quick mitigation — force fallback to flash variant when seq_len>1024 or batch<4. patch suggestion: change prefer order to ["flash","fused_v2"] for those cases. low-risk and fast to test.

sarah: tried that on the same repro (flip prefer -> flash when seq>1024). numbers:
```
before: p99 latency decode step = 118ms
after:  p99 latency decode step = 78ms
kv_write kernel drop from 33.8ms -> 8.5ms
TOTAL GPU time ~82ms -> ~57ms
```

jesse: nvprof confirm: store throughput went up, L1 stall cycles down ~4x. looks like fused_v2 tiling causes partial-store thrashing at these shapes.

alex: good catch. long-term fix options: 1) change fused_v2 write tile to be seq-aligned (padding or vector-friendly layout), 2) add auto-repack for KV to 16B lanes before kernel, 3) keep policy-based fallback.

santiago: agreed. i will open a perf issue with traces + ncu logs. will also add a small unit test that exercises seq=1536, batch=2 to catch regressions.

morgan: sgtm. can you name the issue with tags `perf,kv,attn-tiling` and assign to alex+jesse?

santiago: done. issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/6789 — added timeline and nsys artifact.

sarah: post-fix note: made a tiny policy change in staging to fallback for seq>1024 until we ship tile fix. no customer impact so far. :thumbsup:

santiago: thanks all. follow-ups: alex to prototype tile-change, jesse to validate counters, sarah to monitor staging traces. i'll keep thread updated.
